en.title: Villeneuve 'Deeply Disappointed' by Marvel's 'Dunesday' Release Date Clash
en.summary: Denis Villeneuve is expressing frustration over Marvel's decision to pit "Avengers: Doomsday" against "Dune: Part Three" on December 18, 2026. The "Dune" director feels the move, which creates a cinematic showdown dubbed "Dunesday," is an unnecessary flex that complicates his film's established IMAX release plans.
en.body:
The cinematic calendar for December 2026 just got a whole lot more crowded, and not in a way that director Denis Villeneuve finds particularly welcome. Disney's decision to shift Marvel Studios' "Avengers: Doomsday" to December 18, 2026, directly challenging Warner Bros.' already-slated "Dune: Part Three" on the same date, has stirred significant commentary. This clash, already nicknamed "Dunesday" by industry watchers, has left the "Dune" filmmaker feeling less than thrilled.

Villeneuve, speaking in a recent TIME feature, didn't mince words about his disappointment. He revealed that the decision was "deeply disappointing," particularly given the challenges his "Dune" films have already faced. The first "Dune" navigated a difficult release during the tail end of the COVID-19 pandemic, and "Dune: Part Two" had its own release date shuffled due to the 2023 WGA and SAG-AFTRA strikes. Now, with "Dune: Part Three" having secured its December 18, 2026, date, which was also earmarked for an IMAX release, the arrival of "Avengers: Doomsday" feels like an unwelcome, aggressive move. Villeneuve expressed a hope that both films could "survive" the competition, acknowledging the potential for a massive box office event.

## The 'Dunesday' Showdown

This isn't just a minor scheduling conflict; it's a prime example of studio warfare playing out on the release calendar. Warner Bros. had initially claimed December 18, 2026, for "Dune: Part Three," envisioning it as a triumphant, relatively unchallenged close to the year for their ambitious sci-fi saga. The move by Disney to place their own massive franchise tentpole, "Avengers: Doomsday," on the exact same day is seen by many as a deliberate flex, a "ridiculous, perhaps unnecessary" maneuver during an already busy holiday window. For fans, this means a difficult choice or a marathon viewing experience, but for the filmmakers and studios, it represents a direct battle for box office dominance and audience attention.

## What This Means for Fans

For the passionate global audience of "Dune" and Marvel, "Dunesday" presents an unprecedented cinematic event. While the idea of seeing two of the biggest franchises of the decade on the same day might excite some, it also creates significant logistical and financial considerations for moviegoers. The potential for fractured box office returns, while perhaps a win for Disney in terms of disrupting a rival, could impact the overall success narrative for "Dune: Part Three," a film that has already overcome significant hurdles. Villeneuve's candid frustration underscores the delicate balance of creative ambition and commercial strategy in the blockbuster landscape, leaving fans to wonder how this epic clash will ultimately play out.

## What's Next

"Dune: Part Three" is currently slated for a December 18, 2026 release, with "Avengers: Doomsday" also targeting the same date. Further details on promotional strategies and potential adjustments from either studio have not yet been announced.

See, WB claimed the date first for Dune: Part Three , and with no other serious theatrical competition in sight it looked as though Dune might close out 2026 on a franchise high, unchallenged. Then, like a belligerent three-year-old chucking their plate of chicken nuggies across the Thanksgiving dinner table, Disney shifted the release of Avengers: Doomsday from May 2026 to December 18, prompting entertainment wonks to refer to the day as “Dunesday.”  While we don’t doubt there are plenty of moviegoers out there who have set Dunesday plans to watch Dune: Part Three before (or maybe even instead of) Avengers: Doomsday (as suggested by the star of both films, Florence Pugh), Disney’s provocative date shift has Dune: Part Three director Denis Villeneuve feeling a touch peeved. In a new Time feature released on Friday , Villeneuve expressed frustration over Doomsday ‘s release-date switcheroo, given the uphill fight he and Warner Bros. faced in releasing their first two Dune films, with the first Dune being pushed to October 2021 from its original December 2020 release date due to the COVID pandemic, and the release of Dune: Part Two getting shuffled around amid the SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes of 2023.  “Listen, I will be honest,” Villeneuve said. “The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I said to myself, ‘Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.’ Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth […] So I was deeply disappointed.” After getting that particular grievance off his chest, Villeneuve went on to say that while he’s curbed hopes that Dune might outperform the Marvel film, he believes Dune ‘s “sexiness” sets the genre film apart from its competition. “We had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers , but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex.
